data.summary: The gateway directory contains the Caddy reverse-proxy configuration that fronts the sandbox workloads, exposing code-server and noVNC endpoints on port 8080 behind a single HTTP entrypoint. It is an infrastructure/edge-routing layer rather than business logic, defining per-sandbox upstream targets and path-rewriting rules. It is small but operationally critical because it is the only route into the sandboxed application services.

file_insights.name: Caddyfile
file_insights.summary: Caddy server configuration that exposes code-server and VNC paths on :8080 and reverse-proxies them to the per-sandbox app alias, with header caching overrides for noVNC.
file_insights.source_summary: A declarative Caddy site block for :8080 containing two handle_path routes: /code-server/* reverse-proxied to sbx-devvv-app:8200, and /vnc/* reverse-proxied to the same upstream with no-store cache-control headers forced for unversioned noVNC assets. Comments document the sandbox-mgr generation source, the removal of authentication, and the reason for the unique upstream alias.
file_insights.detailed_description: This Caddyfile is generated by sandbox-mgr for the sandbox gateway and deliberately omits auth (design D9) while mirroring the production repo's route shape. It binds port 8080 and uses handle_path directives so that /code-server/* and /vnc/* prefixes are stripped and forwarded to the uniquely-named per-sandbox upstream sbx-devvv-app (chosen because the bare 'app' alias is ambiguous on the shared aio-mgr-net). It also adds response-header/caching manipulation so noVNC's unversioned relative assets cannot be served stale and crash the client. Because it is the single ingress definition, a mistake here breaks all interactive access to the sandbox.
responsibilities: Terminate the sandbox HTTP edge on port 8080
Strip path prefixes and reverse-proxy requests to the per-sandbox app upstream
Route /code-server/* traffic to the code-server backend
Route /vnc/* traffic to the noVNC backend while forcing no-store caching
